rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable enterprise persona — Salesforce admin/developer or Salesforce consultancy — who demonstrably has budget authority and bills their time at $100–200/hr, making $50–200/mo SaaS pricing plausible. However, operational_autonomy scores 6 (below the 7 build_gate floor): while Claude can diagnose AMPscript/Apex errors from logs, truly useful enterprise debugging requires ongoing integration with Salesforce orgs via OAuth/API, which needs careful per-tenant setup and periodic credential maintenance beyond simple automation. Validate first by offering a manual diagnostic intake (email logs → Claude analysis → recommendations) to test whether enterprise buyers will pay before investing in API-connected automation.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a Salesforce cross-cloud error diagnostic assistant: developers paste their error logs, stack traces, and code snippets into a form and receive a prioritized fix guide within minutes. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt (trained on Salesforce AMPscript/Apex/Marketing Cloud error patterns) + a Typeform or Tally intake form + a Stripe payment link ($49–99/report or $149/mo subscription) + automated email delivery of the diagnosis PDF — no coding by Youval. Outreach targets Salesforce developer communities (Salesforce Stack Exchange, Trailblazer Community, LinkedIn Salesforce developer groups) and Salesforce consulting agencies; the factory drafts and queues all outreach messages for Youval's one-time approval before sending. Delivery is fully automated: form submission triggers Claude analysis → formatted report → emailed to the buyer; Stripe handles billing. The only recurring human touch is Youval approving outreach batches and any edge-case refund requests. Note: if the opportunity grows beyond single-report sales into an always-on org-connected diagnostic tool, it would require OAuth integrations that add meaningful setup complexity.
notes: operational_autonomy (6) is below the build_gate floor of 7 — capped at validate. Org-connected integrations would push autonomy lower; the report-based delivery model keeps it viable.
